items.q: Why do some people speak slowly even when they "know" the answer?
items.a: Two separate issues: **mouth can't keep up with thoughts**, or **brain can't formulate in real time**. If processing lags, you can't formulate responses live — so both halves need **separate drills**, not mindset fluff.

items.q: How do tongue twisters help you speak faster without mumbling?
items.a: Use a **top-50 list**; read one **five times**, accelerating each pass. Twisters **trip you up on purpose** so articulation and velocity train together — speed without hardware becomes mumble.

items.q: How do you measure and raise your rate of speech?
items.a: Take a **300-word story**, time yourself to **1 minute**, count words spoken, then add ~**10 WPM per session** until you plateau — then return to tongue twisters.

items.q: How does breath control make you faster?
items.a: Expelling **too much air per word** forces extra breaths and slows you. Practice **S-sound sustain** and counting **1–20 on one breath** with equal energy per number — avoid collapsing into vocal fry.

items.q: Why do new experts stall on simple questions?
items.a: Slow answers often mean **shallow domain knowledge**. Read **3–5 books** on your specialty so you respond from **understanding**, not memory retrieval.

items.q: How does the 3-2-1 framework stop expert brain meltdown?
items.a: Even deep experts melt without structure. Pick **three steps, two types, or the one thing** — e.g. "record yourself for self-awareness" — instead of dumping everything. **One powerful answer** beats tab-overload.

items.q: What do you do about anxiety taxing cognition?
items.a: Stress **impairs clear thinking**. Prep with diaphragmatic breathing and **box breathing** (Navy SEAL **4-4-4-4**, 3–5 cycles) before high-stakes conversations.
